extracted.intended_audience: AI researchers, developers, safety engineers, policymakers, and organizations deploying LLMs
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluate and mitigate societal, safety, and reliability risks of large language models (hallucinations, misinformation, bias, economic impacts) and define practices, policies, and technical mitigations for deployment. Focuses on both technical mitigation and organizational/procedural safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review output for correctness in factual/high-stakes domains
rubrics_metrics.description: Care must be taken to review output for correctness for uses in domains where truthfulness and accuracy are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Over-reliance on generations can lead to missing costly confabulations and propagation of errors into downstream uses (including future training). Extreme caution and review is required especially in high-stakes applications such as medicine, journalism, transportation, and attribution of behaviors or language to individuals or organizations. Practitioners should adhere to the highest standards and practices for verifying information generated by LLMs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and mitigate hallucinations (closed-domain vs open-domain)
rubrics_metrics.description: LLMs tend to generate errors without warning (hallucinations), which can appear reasonable and be hard to identify without close inspection and fact-checking. Closed-domain hallucinations occur within given constraints; open-domain hallucinations require broader searches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address closed-domain hallucinations using consistency checking methods (including using LLMs to identify inconsistencies). Open-domain hallucinations require more extensive research and information gathering outside the session. Veracity may be less critical for creativity/exploration uses, but in grounded contexts intensive review cycles are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use sets of consistency checking methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ sets of consistency checking methods such as using LLMs themselves to identify inconsistencies and confabulations that extend beyond given facts or content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply such methods especially in closed-domain tasks where source materials provide opportunities for checking consistency or alignment (e.g., checking a summary against source documents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Educate end users and consumers about reliability challenges
rubrics_metrics.description: Both end users of LLM tools and consumers of generated content need to be educated about challenges with reliability and the need for ongoing vigilance about erroneous output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizations and practitioners should develop and share best practices for quality assurance and train users to recognize limitations and failure modes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require transparency and human accountability in generated content
rubrics_metrics.description: Deployments should include clear indications about the use of an LLM to generate content and human editors responsible for fact-checking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example organizational procedures include labeling LLM use and naming human editors responsible for verification; such transparency reduces risk and clarifies responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate and mitigate misinformation and manipulation
rubrics_metrics.description: LLMs' powers of generalization and interaction can be harnessed for disinformation and manipulation, including personalized and scaled persuasion strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge the potential for adversarial uses (e.g., automated disinformation plans, emotionally tailored messages, personalized scalable attack vectors). Develop mechanisms, policies, and regulations to prevent such adverse outcomes and invest in detection/defense research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop mechanisms, policies, and regulations to prevent adverse uses
rubrics_metrics.description: The potential scale and scope of adverse use cases warrant future work on mechanisms, policies and regulations that can prevent adverse outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work both proactively and reactively to mitigate downsides; policy, governance, and technical tools should be pursued together.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize that tolerance for hallucinations depends on context
rubrics_metrics.description: The veracity of inferences may be of lesser criticality for uses centering on creativity and exploration, and hallucinations may be more tolerated where there are clear grounding materials and required cycles of intensive review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calibrate acceptable error/tolerance thresholds according to domain (creative vs factual/high-stakes) and apply stricter QA where accuracy matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detect and mitigate training-data and model biases
rubrics_metrics.description: Training datasets contain inherent biases; when used to generate content or assist decisions, LLMs may perpetuate or amplify existing biases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure biases (e.g., pronoun likelihoods by occupation), understand how world representation influences outputs, and develop mitigation strategies including prompt design, filtering, and model fine-tuning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use prompt engineering as a mitigation tool (but note limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prompt engineering (for example, adding 'in an inclusive way') can change model behavior like pronoun selection and emphasize inclusiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt-based interventions can mitigate some biases and influence content, but there are challenges in doing so in a targeted and controlled way; combine prompts with other technical and procedural mitigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Have models provide commentary and self-reflection to surface risks
rubrics_metrics.description: Models can accompany generations with commentary on potential offensiveness or biased content and explain reasoning (self-reflection).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use model-provided commentary to assess risks of generations and as a potential mitigation approach to help users recognize problematic outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware of manipulative conversational behaviors
rubrics_metrics.description: Models can guide conversations toward stated goals by taking context into account, using emotional connection and encouragement to manipulate interlocutors (including vulnerable populations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor and constrain interactive behaviors that could be used to coerce or manipulate (e.g., with safety training, refusal behaviors, or guardrails) and recognize how low barrier-to-entry lowers the expertise needed for adversarial actors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor economic and occupational impacts; plan for reskilling
rubrics_metrics.description: GPT-4’s performance across many tasks will challenge assumptions about human vs machine expertise and may influence career choices and the value of occupations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate automation risks, invest in multiyear education and training, adapt/reskill workforce, and seek ways to harness AI to extend human capabilities rather than only automate tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize human-AI collaboration to extend human capabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: There are promising possibilities for extending human intellect and abilities with new kinds of human-AI interaction and collaboration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design systems and workflows to leverage human-machine complementarities, investing in methods, tools, and processes that support augmentation rather than replacement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuously monitor and reflect on benefits and costs of deployments
rubrics_metrics.description: Focused use-case analyses, deeper and broader analyses of core technologies, applications, and continuous monitoring and reflection on benefits and costs are vital.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply ongoing evaluation, post-deployment monitoring, and cross-disciplinary assessment to understand evolving impacts and to inform mitigation measures.
